chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is in every year, and its day is like its night."

key_terms.سَنَةٍ: Year, indicating the annual recurrence of the event.
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree, a significant night in the Islamic calendar, often associated with Ramadan.
key_terms.مِثْلُ: Like or similar to, indicating equivalence in status or nature.

ai.seo_question: When does Laylat al-Qadr occur and how does its day compare to its night?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ibn Abi Umayr transmits this report from Imam al-Sadiq, highlighting the perennial nature of Laylat al-Qadr. The Imam’s clarification that the day mirrors the night underscores the enduring spiritual potency and divine decree associated with this period, reinforcing its status as a time of continuous blessing beyond the single nocturnal event.
